maria (SDK): Quick follow-up on the hybrid paging/stream proposal. I sketched APIs for Python/TS/Go so teams can opt into token-streaming or stable page-based iteration with clear retry semantics. PTAL

maria (SDK): Proposed minimal shapes – keep ergonomics similar across langs:
```py
# python
resp = client.generate_stream(prompt)
for chunk in resp:  # yields tokens or token batches
    handle(chunk)
\n# paged
for page in client.generate_pages(prompt, page_size=256):
    process(page)
```
```ts
// ts
const s = client.generateStream(prompt)
for await (const chunk of s) handle(chunk)
\nfor await (const page of client.generatePages(prompt, {pageSize:256})) process(page)
```
```go
// go
stream, _ := client.GenerateStream(ctx, req)
for stream.Scan() { tok := stream.Token(); ... }
\npages := client.GeneratePages(ctx, req)
for pages.Next() { p := pages.Page(); ... }
```

maria (SDK): Key intent: same conceptual model everywhere, but explicit opt-in for resumable pagination. Streams are ephemeral (no resume token). Pages are resumable and have idempotency token.

dan (runtime): How do retries interact? If a page fetch fails mid-page do we retry the page request (idempotent) or surface partial page to caller?

maria (SDK): Page fetches are retried server-side by default using the idempotency token. Client will expose a per-call RetryPolicy to override (fail-fast vs aggressive). We don't re-stream partial token sequences; we resume at page boundary.

ashley (product): Telemetry ask: can we tag requests with "streaming=true|false" and attach fallback reason when we switch from stream->page or vice versa? We need that for cost/quality analysis.

ryan (eng): Transport choice: prefer gRPC streaming for internal low-latency streaming, but clients on browsers need WS/Fetch fallback. Suggest we standardize transport abstraction: Transport.Stream, Transport.PagedFetch. The SDK maps to best transport available.

maria (SDK): Agreed. Impl plan: default to gRPC if env supports it, otherwise HTTP chunked streaming. We'll surface that mapping in docs and expose Transport.hints for advanced users.

ryan (eng): Back-compat: older clients expect single-call generate() returning full text. We should keep that wrapper that buffers stream into complete response. Mark streaming API as stable v1.0, paged API as experimental until we validate resume tokens.

maria (SDK): For semver, we version streaming/paged features independently: streaming is additive (no break), paged resume token format in headers will carry a schema version. Clients parse and fail gracefully if unknown.

ashley (product): Decision checklist: (1) streaming + wrapper for full response, (2) paged with idempotency + resume token, (3) per-call RetryPolicy exposed, (4) transport hints + telemetry tags. Anyone opposed?

ryan (eng): +1 from infra, but need an RFC doc with failure cases (partial pages, token mismatch) and perf numbers.

maria (SDK): I'll draft RFC with API signatures, sample code, and a small compatibility matrix. Will include a tiny integration test plan.

ci-bot: CI: perf-tests/hybrid-pager completed: 4/5 flakes passed, baseline latency for stream path: 40ms p50, paged path: 120ms p50. Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/1828790123

maria (SDK): Nice — I'll include those numbers. Plan to ship an experimental SDK PR next week and feature-flag paged resume for alpha users.

ryan (eng): Cool. Assigning follow-ups: @maria to draft RFC, @dan to spec server retry contract, @ashley to define telemetry fields. We can sync Monday.
